Model year: 2027 (26/27 season) [2] 4. Product type: Freeride snowboard [3] 5. Gender: Men's [4] 6. Founder: Jeremy Jones, professional freeride snowboarder [5] 7. Company founded: 2009–2010 (sources disagree; Wikipedia says 2010, other sources say 2009) [5][6] — DISAGREEMENT: Wikipedia and Cirkel Supply say "founded in 2010," while Boardertown and Grokipedia say "2009." The discrepancy likely reflects announcement (2009) vs. first product availability (2010–11 season). 8. Parent company: Nidecker Group (NDK Group), which also owns Nidecker, Flow, YES., and Now [7] 9. Headquarters: Truckee, California, near Lake Tahoe [8] 10. Corporate entity: Jones – Nidecker US Inc, 11253 Brockway Rd Suite E202, Truckee, CA [9] 11. Brand manager: Xavier Nidecker [10] 12. Manufacturing location: SWS (Solico Winter Sport) factory, Dubai, UAE [11] 13. SWS factory background: Set up by former Elan factory workers; produces ~300,000 boards/year for multiple brands [12] 14. Fair Trade Certified: Jones snowboards and splitboards are Fair Trade Certified — an industry first for hard goods [13] 15. Manufacturing powered by 100% solar energy [14] 16. 1% for the Planet member: Jones donates 1% of sales to sustainability-focused non-profits [15] 17. Flagship model first sold: 2010–11 season (part of Jones' inaugural four-board lineup along with Mountain Twin, Hovercraft, Solution) [16] 18. Predecessor model continuity: The 2026 Jones Flagship had no changes from 2025; 2024 and 2025 got stiffer flex and a new topsheet vs. 2017–2023 models [17] 19. 2027 model updates: Subtle shaping refinements, updated graphics, and small performance tweaks; no radical redesign [18] STATUS & AVAILABILITY 20. Price (USD, MSRP): $749.95 [9] 36. Flagship Pro MSRP: $899.95 USD [9] 37. Warranty: 2+1 warranty (free warranty extension on all boards when product is registered) [9] SHAPE & PROFILE 38. Shape: Tapered Directional (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] 39. Shape description: Directional outline with a longer nose and shorter tail for stability, float, and confidence [27] 40. Camber type: Directional Camber/Rocker — camber throughout body with rocker in the nose (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] 41. Camber description: Camber-dominant profile; camber runs from the front binding through the tail; nose rises freely in powder [28] 42. Taper: 12mm across all sizes (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] — Note: The merchant lists 12mm for the 2027 model, but the Jones official website shows varying taper by size (12–14mm range depending on size) [9]. This is a DISAGREEMENT; the merchant's spec may apply to a subset of sizes. 43. Taper (Jones official, 161cm): 12.0mm [9] 44. Taper (Jones official, 151cm): 14.0mm [9] 45. Setback: 20mm across all sizes (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] 46. Nose design: Blunt nose for improved powder float without extra swing weight [29] BASE & 3D TECHNOLOGY 47. 3D contour base: High 3D Contour Base with 7mm spoon bevel in nose and up to 7mm in tail, starting just before contact points (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] 48. 3D Contour Base version: 3D Contour Base 3.0 — Jones' most aggressive base contour [28] 49. Base material (merchant-verified): Sintered 8000 Base [MERCHANT] 50. Base material (Ballistyx description): Sintered 8000 — durable, high-density sintered base that absorbs wax effectively [30] 51. Base material DISAGREEMENT: The Jones official website and evo list "Sintered 9900 Base" for the current (2025/2026) Flagship. The merchant and Ballistyx list "Sintered 8000" for the 2027 model. This may represent a spec change for 2027 or a data discrepancy. [9][30][MERCHANT] 52. Flip-Flop Base: Two base colorways to minimize P-Tex waste; color may vary [9] 53. Base contouring: 3D Base Contouring inspired by surfboard design, reduces tip drag (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] CONSTRUCTION & MATERIALS 54. Core material: Control Core — dual-density full premium wood, 2:1 paulownia to poplar stringer ratio (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] 55. Core (Jones official): Power Core — advanced triple-density full wood core made from responsibly harvested Bamboo, Paulownia and Poplar [9] 56. Core DISAGREEMENT: The merchant lists "Control Core (dual-density, paulownia to poplar)" while Jones' official site describes "Power Core (triple-density, Bamboo, Paulownia, Poplar)." This may reflect a 2027 update or naming difference. [MERCHANT][9] 57. Laminate: Triax Fiberglass — triaxial, triple-layer, multi-axis construction (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] 58. Carbon reinforcement: BComp Carbon Flax Stringer with Bio Resin (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] 59. BComp stringer description: Carbon provides pop; flax absorbs chatter and reduces CO₂ vs. full carbon stringer [9] 60. Resin: Plant-based bio resin — 27% plant-based carbon instead of petroleum-based carbon, reduces CO₂ by 33% (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] 61. Topsheet: Ash Wood Veneer — lightweight, super damp, eliminates edge chatter, delivers even flex [9] 62. Topsheet (merchant-verified): Premium Topsheet (durable and scratch resistant) [MERCHANT] 63. Sidewall material: Recycled ABS with round finish (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] 64. Sidewall description: Rounded finish engineered to reduce topsheet chipping and impact damage [9] 65. Edges: Recycled German steel edges (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] 66. Edge technology: Traction Tech — strategically placed contact points for enhanced edge grip (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] 67. Traction Tech version: Traction Tech 3.0 — locks in three contact points per edge for maximum grip [28] 68. Factory wax: WEND Natural Wax — ready to ride out of the shop (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] 69. Factory tuning: Factory detuned in tip and tail, ready to ride (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] 70. Flex conditioning: Forever Flex — overbuilt then broken in at the factory to mimic 20 days ridden (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] 71. Mounting pattern: 2x4 Inserts (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] 72. Extra inserts: Float Pack — extra set of inserts for setback stance in deep powder (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] FLEX & PERFORMANCE RATINGS 73. Flex rating: 8/10 (stiff) (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] 74. Flex (Jones official): Mid-stiff & lively, 4/5 on Jones scale [9] 75. Flex (evo scale): 4/5 (1 = Soft and Playful, 5 = Stiff and Aggressive) [29] 76. Flex (The Ski Monster): Stiff (8 out of 10) [31] 77. All mountain rating: 9/10 (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] 78. Jones official on-piste/all-mountain rating: 7/10 [9] 79. DISAGREEMENT on all-mountain rating: Merchant rates 9/10; Jones official site rates 7/10 for on-piste/all-mountain. Different rating systems — merchant may combine freeride versatility; Jones separates categories. 80. Powder rating: 10/10 (merchant-verified) [MERCHANT] 81. Board weight 158cm: 2.9kg / 6.5lbs [9] REVIEW OPINIONS & RIDE CHARACTERISTICS 120. User rating on Jones website: 4.8/5 (459 reviews) [9] 121. Review: SnowboardingProfiles ranked the Flagship #1 in their top freeride snowboards list for 2025–2026 [34] 122. Review positive: Excellent stability at speed — "nice and stable at speed, which was no surprise" [33] 123. Review positive: Fast base glide — "really fast base - and the glide was excellent" [33] 124. Review positive: Outstanding in crud/chunder — "hardly felt any chatter going through a large patch of icy chunder" [33] 125. Review positive: Excellent dampening — ash wood veneer topsheet and BComp stringers absorb chatter [28] 126. Review positive: Surprisingly nimble in tight terrain despite stiffness [31] 127. Review positive: Forgiving for its stiffness — easy to skid a turn when needed [17] 128. Review positive: Excellent powder float from directional shape, taper, setback, and 3D base contouring [33] 129. Review positive: Build quality is solid — "nothing rattles, nothing feels cheap" [35] 130. Review positive: Feels like a board you buy to keep for years [35] 131. Review negative: Not suitable for park or jibbing [33] 132. Review negative: Reference stance is very wide — a noted concern by The Good Ride [17] 133. Review negative: Float Pack setback inserts are far apart, limiting usability for some riders [17] 134. Review negative: Can feel "a touch washy" on hard carving turns due to spoon tech/lifted edges [17] 135. Review negative: Pop requires effort — "you have to load the tail properly" [35] 136. Review negative: High price limits value unless freeride is your primary use [36] 137. Review negative: Topsheet can show cosmetic wear after use, though not severe [37] 138. Ride characteristic — on snow feel: Stable [17] 139. Ride characteristic — turn initiation: Medium/Fast [17] 140. Ride characteristic — skidded turns: Semi-Easy [17] 141. Ride characteristic — buttering: Semi-Hard [17] 142. Ride characteristic — edge hold: Hard snow capable [17] 143. Ride characteristic — speed: Great — "doesn't have a speed limit" [31] 144. Ride characteristic — powder: Great [17] 145. Ride characteristic — switch riding: Average [17] 146. Ride characteristic — jumps: Good [17] 147. Ride characteristic — jibbing: Poor [17] 148. Ride characteristic — pipe: Good [17] 149. Perceived weight: Feels normal — a little heavier than average on scales but normal on snow [33] COMPETITOR COMPARISONS 150. Similar boards (The Good Ride): Amplid Souly Grail, K2 Alchemist, YES PYL Uninc, Weston Backwoods, Cardiff Powgoda, United Shapes Cadet [17] 151. Jones Stratos comparison: Stratos is the all-conditions hybrid (7/10 flex); Flagship steps up with 8/10 flex and more focused freeride personality [28] 152. Jones Flagship Pro comparison: Pro adds Koroyd nose dampening, Carbon/Innegra reinforcement, Power Plates, and 5/5 flex; aimed at expert riders [28] 153. Flagship Pro price: $899.95 vs. $749.95 for standard — The Good Ride suggests Pro is worth the upgrade [17] 154. Flagship vs. Burton Flight Attendant: Both are versatile freeride boards; Flagship edges out on powder float and base speed [17] 155. Flagship vs. YES Pick Your Line: Both are freeride favorites; PYL is considered better value for money [34] 156. Flagship vs. Never Summer Valhalla: Valhalla rated #2 freeride board by SnowboardingProfiles; more versatile across speed ranges [34] 157. The Good Ride 2026 Freeride Favorites: Lists Flagship Pro as a top freeride board [38] SUSTAINABILITY & ETHICS 158. Bio Resin: 27% plant-based carbon, 33% less greenhouse gas emissions than conventional epoxy [9] 159. Recycled ABS sidewalls: Uses only recycled plastic [9] 160. Recycled steel edges: Made from recycled German steel [9] 161. FSC-certified wood core: Responsibly harvested materials [9] 162. Re-Up program: Dead boards can be recycled for $50 toward a new one [9] 163. Fair Trade Certified factory: SWS Dubai factory certified for worker empowerment, fair wages [13] 164. 100% solar-powered manufacturing and headquarters [13] RETAILER REPUTATION NOTES 165. Jones Snowboards direct: Manufacturer store; most authoritative; free shipping >$100 US, 30-day returns on unused items [9] 166. evo: Major US outdoor retailer, price match guarantee (beat by 5%), well-regarded [23] 167. REI: Major US outdoor co-op, strong return policy, trusted retailer [25] 168. Backcountry: Major US specialty retailer; well-known for snow sports [24] 169. Tactics: Core boardshop, well-regarded in snowboard community [24] 170. Twelve Board Store: Australian authorized Jones dealer; free shipping Australia-wide, price matching [21] 171. Ballistyx: Trusted Melbourne snowboard store since 1991; authorized Jones dealer [22] 172. Milosport: Established Salt Lake City boardshop; in-store pickup available [19] 173. The Ski Monster: Boston-based specialty shop; expert staff testing all products [31]
